newsitem.title: UK: Britain's BT-MCI merger would save 1.5 bln pounds.
newsitem.headline: Britain's BT-MCI merger would save 1.5 bln pounds.

text.p: British Telecommunications Plc said on Sunday its planned merger with MCI Communications Corp, the number two U.S. long-distance phone company, would yield savings of 1.5 billion pounds ($2.46 billion) over five years.
BT, the dominant player in the British telecoms market, said it expected annual pre-tax synergy savings of about 500 million pounds by the fifth year following the merger.

In the statement detailing the deal which started leaking into the markets late on Friday, BT also forecast dividends of 19.85p per share for the year to March 31, 1997 -- a rise of six percent over last year -- excluding a 35p per share special dividend.
BT, which will release full year results on November 14, has declared a half year dividend of 7.90 pence payable in November, six percent more than in the same period last year.

Accordingly, the final dividend will be 11.95 pence per share. "BT's board believes that its earnings and cash flow will continue to be strong enough to support a growing dividend (as adjusted for the effect of the special dividend)," it stated.
"The intention will be to grow earnings at a higher level, which would lead to an increase in dividend cover over time."
BT said that if its merger plans won regulatory clearance, its debt-to-equity ratio, or gearing, would stand at about 65 percent.

The enlarged group would thus be able to maintain substantial capital expenditure in existing operations as well as investing for growth in new markets, while continuing a competitive dividend policy, being able to buy back shares and reducing gearing over time, BT said.
The company will seek shareholder approval to buy back 10 percent of its own shares at an extraordinary meeting to approve the merger.

BT, which is giving shareholders a 35 pence per share special dividend bonanza as part of the deal, is keen to distribute cash to investors to increase its borrowing and make it more capital efficient.
BT already has a 20 percent stake in MCI. The two also operate a joint venture known as Concert which serves customers in more than 50 nations.
The merged company will be called Concert Plc.

"The addition of MCI profits and the incremental profits arising from teh extra revenues and reduced costs are anticipated to generate earnings growth at Concert comforably superior to that which BT could achieve on its own," BT stated.

However, with the special dividend alone being worth an estimated 2.0 billion pounds, the merger is expected to lead to "modest" earnings dilution in the year to March 31, 1998, it noted. ($1=.6096 Pound)
